newsitem.title: USA: Norwest "unlikely" to buy investment bank.
newsitem.headline: Norwest "unlikely" to buy investment bank.

text.p: Norwest Corp, an $80.2 billion financial services company, said Wednesday it is not likely to acquire an investment bank similar to BankAmerica Corp's recent decision to buy Robertson Stephens & Co.

"I don't think it's likely we will do something like that," Richard Kovacevich, Norwest chairman and chief executive, told a Piper Jaffray investment conference here. "It's not impossible, but unlikely."
Earlier this month, BankAmerica Corp said it would acquire Robertson Stephens in a deal valued at $540 million.

It was the latest deal between a commercial bank and investment bank as a result of easing of restrictions by the Federal Reserve and other regulators on commercial banks' ability to engage in brokerage activities.
Kovacevich defined Norwest's position as a distributor of banking, investment and insurance products and services seeking to capture a greater market share in each of these financial services.
Norwest's stock trading symbol, NOB, stands for 'Not Only Banking,' he said.

He said Norwest is similar to other distributors like McDonald's, Wal-Mart, Home Depot and Starbucks. These companies operate in large fragmented industries, selling commodities with unique distribution systems and successfully expanding first regionally and then nationally.

He identified Prudential as the leader in financial services with only a 2.2 percent share of an estimated $1.86 trillion market, Wal-Mart as the leader with a 42.7 percent share of the $175 billion general merchandise market, and McDonald's the leader with a 19 percent share of the $157 billion fast food market.
"Growth by increasing market share is an incredible opportunity," in financial services, he said.

Norwest's plan to boost its market share includes opening new stores, creating new channels of distribution, selling more products and services in existing channels, and selling more products and services to existing customers using information based on a highly developed customer database.
